title: Confident not-anomalous answer with a high ambiguity flag is silenced instead of escalated
detail: Rule 4 (confident-not-anomalous -> ignore) runs before rule 5 (high-ambiguity -> escalate). An answer that says 'not-anomalous' at confidence 0.9 while flagging ambiguity 0.99 routes to 'ignore' (confirmed: routeItem({answer:{kind:'not-anomalous',confidence:0.9,ambiguity:0.99}}) -> ignore). That is an uncertain item taking a silent route, which breaks the idea's core rule that a wrong silence is not recoverable. It is also inconsistent: suppress or fix at 0.99 with the same ambiguity escalates (line 86), so the not-anomalous path is the only silent route that skips the ambiguity check. The test at test/kit-asymmetric-threshold-router.test.js:44 locks this silence in, and the 'silent routes' property test (line 97) checks only confidence, not ambiguity. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/threshold-route.js:85.
fix_hint: Require ambiguity < high (or ambiguity absent) for the ignore route, for example by adding `&& !(a.ambiguity >= high)` to line 85, so a high-ambiguity not-anomalous answer escalates. Flip the test at line 44 to expect 'escalate', and add ambiguity to the silent-routes property test.

title: One malformed model answer anywhere in the batch drops every deterministic block
detail: routeAll validates every item before it routes any of them. checkItem also validates the answer on a ledger or regression item (line 69-74, test line 187). So a single model answer with confidence 95 (a 0-100 scale), a string '0.9', or a null ambiguity makes the whole call exit 1 with no results, no `blocks` and no `blocking`. Confirmed: routeAll([{id:'reg',deterministicRegression:true},{id:'m',answer:{kind:'anomaly',confidence:95}}]) throws, and the program-seen regression on 'reg' is never reported. The idea says a deterministic regression always goes to a blocking check and a model answer cannot override it. Here the model's output shape can suppress the block, and the /w-review target is advisory, so a failed call may just be skipped.
fix_hint: Validate the item's own flags strictly. Treat a malformed answer as a missing answer (route 'ask-human' with a rule such as 'malformed-answer') instead of throwing, so regression items still block. Or route deterministicRegression items before the answer is validated. Add a test where a regression item and a malformed-answer item share a batch and the result still blocks.

title: Non-object thresholds silently fall back to the looser defaults in the module API
detail: autoFixEligible, routeItem and routeAll call resolveThresholds(thresholds || {}). A caller who passes a bare number (routeAll(items, 0.95)) or a string gets the defaults 0.4 / 0.8 with no error, because property reads on a number return undefined. Confirmed: routeAll([...], 0.95).thresholds -> {low:0.4, high:0.8}. A caller who meant a stricter floor then gets auto-fix and suppress at a lower confidence than intended. The CLI path rejects a non-object thresholds value (line 174), but the module entry the integration targets will call does not.
fix_hint: In resolveThresholds, throw exit 1 when t is not undefined and is not a plain object.

title: Findings that did reproduce are still quarantined and never block
detail: Quarantine fires when failures - reproductions >= 2, whatever the reproduction count. A high-severity finding with failures 5 and reproductions 3 (it showed up again on 3 of 5 retries) is quarantined, removed from filed and summary, and blocking is false (checked: plan([{id:'z',severity:'high',failures:5,reproductions:3}]) gives quarantined 1, blocking false). The idea brief says a finding that 'fails to reproduce on two retries' is quarantined. A finding that reproduced is confirmed, so an intermittent real bug is kept out of Ralph work. The packaged test fixes this behaviour in place with failures 3 and reproductions 1. The same logic is in .claude/helpers/kit/noise-ledger.js:142.
fix_hint: Quarantine only when reproductions === 0 && failures >= QUARANTINE_AFTER, or document a ratio rule on purpose. Add a test showing that a finding with reproductions > 0 is filed.

title: --now with a UTC offset uses the local calendar day, not the UTC day
detail: parseDate accepts ISO times with an offset but returns the literal YYYY-MM-DD prefix. With --now 2026-10-15T23:30:00-05:00 (UTC 2026-10-16T04:30Z), the day comes out as 2026-10-15, so a ledger entry that expires on 2026-10-15 still matches (checked: accepted 1). The header says expiry is 'UTC, inclusive', and today() takes the UTC day for a Date object, so the two kinds of --now input disagree near midnight. The same applies to '+0900' offsets. Mirrored in .claude/helpers/kit/noise-ledger.js:48.
fix_hint: When the string has a time part with Z or an offset, return new Date(v).toISOString().slice(0,10). Keep the literal prefix only for a bare date. Add a test for an offset input near midnight.

title: accept/prune rewrite the committed ledger and drop any extra entry or top-level fields
detail: normalizeLedger rebuilds each entry from only id, reason, added and expires, and forces version 1. accept and prune write that result back. A field a team added by hand (for example owner or ticket) disappears silently from the committed file the next time anyone runs accept or prune (checked: an entry with owner and ticket comes back without them). An unknown future version is also rewritten as 1 without a warning.
fix_hint: Spread the original entry (and the top-level object) before the normalised fields when writing, or refuse unknown fields and versions with exit 1 so nothing is lost silently.

title: --in - reads a file named '-' instead of stdin, unlike sibling kit verbs
detail: Other kit verbs treat '-' as stdin: graph and lenses take '--diff -' and safe-git takes '--input -'. noise-ledger apply resolves '--in -' as a path and fails with 'cannot read -: ENOENT'. Someone choosing between the two input methods by habit gets a confusing error.
fix_hint: Treat f.in === '-' as the stdin branch, including the TTY check, or reject it with a message pointing to stdin.

title: "path:line:col" locations are read as file "path:line", which splits one file into many
detail: The location regex /^(.*):(\d+)$/ only strips the last :N. For 'src/a.js:12:5', a format linters, tsc and review agents commonly emit, the file becomes 'src/a.js:12' and the line becomes 5 (confirmed: two findings with the same rule at 'src/a.js:12:5' and 'src/a.js:40:2' get the file sets ['src/a.js:12'] and ['src/a.js:40']). Findings in the same file therefore land in different buckets, their file sets are disjoint, and they are never even offered as a pending pair. The feature fails silently on this input: duplicates stay apart, and the files list names paths that do not exist. The same applies to .claude/helpers/kit/cluster.js:84.
fix_hint: Parse an optional column, /^(.*?):(\d+)(?::\d+)?$/, and keep the column or drop it; add a test with a 'path:line:col' location.

title: One malformed decide() reply aborts the run and discards every judgment already paid for
detail: decide() is the model hook, so its replies are untrusted model output. checkJudgment throws on the first reply that is slightly off (for example confidence 'High', since confidence is case-sensitive while severity is lowercased at line 68, or p given as the string '0.8'). The throw rejects the whole cluster() call: pass-1 results and the verdicts from every earlier decide call are lost, and the caller has nothing to show for the model spend. A null reply already means 'leave the pair pending'. A reply that cannot be read should degrade the same way and never merge, because merging is the risky direction.
fix_hint: In the decide loop, treat a reply that fails checkJudgment as unjudged (leave the pair pending and record it, e.g. in an invalid_judgments list) instead of throwing. Optionally lowercase confidence before validating it.

title: --file with an empty value silently falls back to stdin
detail: `if (file)` treats `--file ''`, for example from an unset shell variable, as if --file were absent. The verb then reads stdin, or fails with 'no findings: pass --file', which hides the real cause. The --answers file has the same problem at line 264: an empty value silently means 'no answers'.
fix_hint: Check `file !== null` / `answersFile !== null` and reject an empty value with 'needs a value'.

title: The /p/ error regex matches almost any message
detail: The malformed-answer check asserts the rejection message matches /p/. Most error texts contain a 'p', so the test would still pass if validation failed for an unrelated reason, such as a missing a/b.
fix_hint: Assert on /"p" must be a number/.

title: Test says equal file sets are never pending but never tests it
detail: The test is named 'a subset file set also counts as overlap-but-different; disjoint and equal do not', but it only checks the subset case and the disjoint case. Equal file sets with the same rule but different input ordering or ./ prefixes are never checked to produce zero pending pairs.
fix_hint: Add an assertion: pass1([f('a','r','low',['x','y']), f('b','r','low',['./y','x'])]) gives one cluster and pending_pairs.length === 0.

title: Concurrent callers silently lose spend (unlocked read-modify-write)
detail: run() does load(file) -> pure update -> save(file) with no lock or compare-and-swap; the atomic rename only prevents torn files, not lost updates. Confirmed: 20 parallel `shared-budget spend --steps 1` processes against one state file all exited 0, but the file ended with spent.steps=10 and 10 helper rows. Half the spend vanished with no error, so the shared allowance under-reports and later grants hand out budget that was already used: sub-sessions overspend. The same race drops grant/skip counts and start/stop depth changes (a lost `start` leaves depth one short, so a later `stop` banks time early or throws 'stop without a matching start'). The idea's stated use is several sub-agents sharing one allowance, so concurrent callers are the normal path. Mirrored in .claude/helpers/kit/shared-budget.js.
fix_hint: Serialize every mutating command with an exclusive lock file (fs.open(file+'.lock','wx') with retry/backoff and stale-lock timeout) held across load..save, and add a test that runs N parallel spends and asserts spent.steps === N.

title: Grants do not reserve budget, so parallel sub-sessions together overspend
detail: grantFor returns the full remaining allowance to every caller and recordGrant only bumps a counter; nothing is held in flight. Confirmed: with --steps 10, three concurrent grants each returned remaining.steps=10, licensing 30 steps against a 10-step limit. The only guard is the after-the-fact `overrun` report. The existing src/lib/marathon/budget.js canFanOut counts in-flight budgets for exactly this reason; this verb drops that, so the 'one allowance shared by several sub-agents' promise does not hold for any fan-out.
fix_hint: Record each grant's reservation (e.g. helpers[id].reserved) and subtract outstanding reservations in remainingOf; release/replace the reservation on spend. Alternatively document that grants are sequential-only and give a --share/--parts option that splits the remainder.

title: Temp file name collides for same-process concurrent saves
detail: save() names the temp file `${file}.${process.pid}.${Date.now()}.tmp`. Two run() calls in the same process within one millisecond (library use, e.g. Promise.all over sub-sessions) write and rename the same temp path. Confirmed: 10 concurrent run(['spend',...]) calls in one process -> 8 rejected with 'cannot write ...: ENOENT', only 2 recorded. The failed spends are lost even though the sub-sessions did the work, contradicting 'spend is recorded at once, failures included'.
fix_hint: Use a unique temp suffix (crypto.randomUUID() or an incrementing counter) and, together with the lock from the first finding, serialize writers.

title: Concurrent accept runs silently lose ledger entries
detail: accept reads the ledger, adds one entry and renames a temp file over the original. Nothing locks the file or checks that it has not changed in between. Two runs at the same time each write their own snapshot, so whichever rename lands last wins. Checked: 8 parallel `cli.js noise-ledger accept --id idN` runs against one ledger all exited 0, and the file ended with only 2 of the 8 entries. Every run reported success, so a user or a parallel swarm agent believes a decision was recorded when it was not. That finding is filed again on the next apply. The same code is mirrored in .claude/helpers/kit/noise-ledger.js:256.
fix_hint: Take an exclusive lock file (fs.open with 'wx') around the read-modify-write and retry or fail with exit 1 while it is held. Or re-read the file just before rename and refuse when its content changed. Add a test that runs parallel accepts and expects all of them kept.

title: Rewrite silently blanks hand-edited reason and drops non-string added
detail: normalizeLedger keeps unknown fields but forces the known ones: a reason that is not a string becomes '' and an added that is not a string becomes undefined, which JSON.stringify then drops. Any accept or prune writes that back to the committed file. Checked: an entry with reason ['line one','line two'] and added 20261001 came back from an unrelated accept as reason "" with no added field. The reason for a suppression is deleted from the committed record without any warning.
fix_hint: Refuse (exit 1) an entry whose reason or added is present but not a string, as is already done for expires, rather than coercing it.

title: Ledger saved with a UTF-8 BOM is rejected as invalid JSON
detail: readLedger passes the raw file text to JSON.parse. The ledger is a committed file that people edit by hand, and several editors save a leading BOM. With one, apply, accept and prune all exit 1 with 'is not valid JSON' even though the content is fine (checked with a BOM-prefixed valid ledger). Because the ledger is read on every apply, the whole advisory step fails until someone finds the invisible character.
fix_hint: Strip a leading \uFEFF before JSON.parse (text.replace(/^\uFEFF/, '')).

title: Mapped share is rounded before the low-confidence comparison, so a share just under the minimum skips the smoke set
detail: mappedPct is pct(), which rounds to one decimal, and line 143 compares that rounded value with minMappedPct. 241 of 402 changed files mapped is 59.95%, which rounds to 60.0. With the default --min-mapped-pct 60 the result is low_confidence false, no smoke set, and mapped_pct 60 (confirmed with planTests). That breaks the rule 'below the threshold, add a smoke set and flag it, never silent'. It only happens on large change sets (about 400 or more files), so it is rare.
fix_hint: Compare the raw ratio: mapped * 100 < minMappedPct * files.length. Keep the rounded value for display only.

title: low_confidence_reason says 'a smoke set was added' when the smoke set is empty
detail: The reason string is fixed text. If no target has entry: true and --smoke is 0, nothing is added: with planTests({targets:[{id:'a',files:[]}]}, ['z.js'], {smoke:0}) the plan is [], yet the reason still says a smoke set was added. A reviewer reading only the reason would think a fallback ran when none did.
fix_hint: Count the targets the smoke step actually added and word the reason to match, e.g. 'smoke set: N targets' or 'no smoke targets available'.

title: Misspelled threshold keys silently fall back to the looser defaults
detail: resolveThresholds reads only t.low and t.high and ignores every other key. The CLI likewise reads only data.items and data.thresholds (line 175-180) and ignores other top-level keys. So a caller who means a stricter floor but writes {"thresholds":{"hi":0.95}}, {"High":0.95} or a top-level "threshold" (singular) gets high = 0.8 with exit 0 and no warning. Confirmed: echo '{"items":[{"answer":{"kind":"suppress","confidence":0.85}}],"thresholds":{"hi":0.95}}' | cli.js threshold-route routes to 'suppress', and the same with "threshold":{"high":0.95} routes a fix at 0.85 to 'auto-fix'. In module form, routeAll(items, {High:0.95}) also suppresses at 0.85. The silent routes then open at a lower confidence than the caller set, which is the one direction this verb exists to prevent. The r1 fix closed the non-object case but not this one. Same code in .claude/helpers/kit/threshold-route.js.
fix_hint: In resolveThresholds, throw exit 1 on any key other than low/high. In run(), throw exit 1 on any top-level key of the object form other than items/thresholds. Add a test for each.

title: A UTF-8 BOM in the input file is rejected as invalid JSON
detail: run() passes the file text straight to JSON.parse, and readFile with 'utf-8' keeps a leading BOM. A JSON file written by a tool that adds a BOM (for example Windows PowerShell Out-File / Set-Content -Encoding utf8) fails with 'input is not valid JSON' and exit 1, so no item is routed and a regression in it never reports 'blocks'. Confirmed with a BOM-prefixed [{"deterministicRegression":true}] passed through --file. The failure is loud, not silent.
fix_hint: Strip a leading \uFEFF before JSON.parse: text.replace(/^\uFEFF/, '').

title: Chained merges join same-rule clusters with disjoint files that pass 1 kept apart
detail: The transitive veto only looks at pairs that are in `pending`, and same-rule clusters with disjoint file sets are never pending. So A{header.tsx,p1.tsx}, B{header.tsx,footer.tsx}, C{footer.tsx,p2.tsx}, with A~B and B~C approved, all collapse into one cluster with representative A (confirmed: clusters [["A",["A","B","C"]]], blocked []). Nobody judged A against C, and pass 1 had settled them as different parts: the header says disjoint clusters 'are never offered for merging', and the test at test/kit-two-pass-finding-clustering.test.js:89 says such a pair 'never merges'. An unjudged overlapping pair vetoes a chain, but a pair pass 1 already called different does not, so the safety rule is weaker exactly where the evidence for 'different' is strongest. C's issue (footer) is then hidden behind A's title (header), which is the outcome the higher merge bar is meant to prevent. The same code is in .claude/helpers/kit/cluster.js:223.
fix_hint: In the veto loop, also veto when x and y share a rule but are not a pending pair (disjoint files), with why 'disjoint'. Or require every cross pair to be an approved pending pair. Add a test for the A-B-C chain above that expects 2 clusters and one blocked entry.

title: Line-range locations ('path:12-14') are taken as part of the file name
detail: The location regex accepts only 'path:line' and 'path:line:col'. A range such as 'src/a.js:12-14' (the form this suite's own bbs evidence lines use, e.g. 'packages/triage/src/cluster.ts:23-46') does not match, so the whole string becomes the file 'src/a.js:12-14' (confirmed). A finding with that location gets a file set that is disjoint from others in src/a.js. It never pairs with them, so the duplicates stay apart without warning, and the files list names a path that does not exist. Same in .claude/helpers/kit/cluster.js:93.
fix_hint: Extend the regex to /^(.*?):(\d+)(?:[-:]\d+)?$/ (take the start line), and add a test with a 'path:start-end' location.

title: BOM fix covers only UTF-8: a UTF-16 findings or answers file from Windows PowerShell 5.1 is reported as 'not valid JSON'
detail: readJsonFile always decodes as utf-8 and strips only U+FEFF. Windows PowerShell 5.1, still the default shell on Windows 10/11, writes UTF-16LE with a BOM for `>` and `Out-File` (for example `ConvertTo-Json | Out-File findings.json`). That is the most common way older Windows tooling produces a BOM file. Confirmed: a UTF-16LE file with a BOM holding a valid one-finding list exits 1 with 'findings file "..." is not valid JSON'. The verb fails loudly, so no wrong result is produced, but the message points the user at the JSON content instead of the encoding, and this round's BOM change suggests Windows-written files are handled. The same applies to .claude/helpers/kit/cluster.js:256.
fix_hint: Read the file as a Buffer. If it starts with FF FE (or FE FF), decode it as utf16le (swap the bytes for BE), otherwise decode it as utf-8 and strip the BOM. Or keep utf-8 and, when the raw bytes start with FF FE or FE FF, throw 'is UTF-16; save it as UTF-8'. Add a test with a UTF-16LE file.

title: UTF-16 input from Windows PowerShell 5.1 still fails as 'input is not valid JSON'
detail: The r2 fix strips only a UTF-8 BOM. Windows PowerShell 5.1, still the default shell on many Windows machines, writes UTF-16LE with an FF FE BOM for Out-File and for the > redirect (e.g. ConvertTo-Json ... > in.json). run() reads the file as utf-8, so the text starts with replacement characters and NUL bytes and JSON.parse fails. Confirmed: a UTF-16LE file holding [{"id":"r","deterministicRegression":true}] passed with --file to .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js threshold-route gives 'kit: input is not valid JSON' and exit 1, so the regression in it never reports blocks. The failure is loud, not silent, and the message gives no hint that the encoding is the problem. Same code in .claude/helpers/kit/threshold-route.js:173.
fix_hint: Read the file (and stdin via io.stdinBytes) as bytes. If it starts with FF FE or FE FF, decode it as UTF-16 (TextDecoder('utf-16le') / ('utf-16be')); otherwise decode as UTF-8 and strip a leading U+FEFF. Or, at least, detect FF FE / FE FF and throw 'input is UTF-16; save it as UTF-8'. Add a test with a UTF-16LE file.

title: Breaking a stale lock lets two runs hold it at once, so accepts are still lost
detail: When the lock is older than LOCK_STALE_MS, every waiter that stats it does an unconditional fs.rm(lock) and then retries. Waiter A can remove the old lock and create its own with 'wx', and waiter B, which saw the same stale mtime, then removes A's fresh lock and creates its own. Both run the read-modify-write together and the last rename wins. The finally block also does an unconditional rm, so a run can delete a lock that another run now holds. Checked: with a stale ledger.json.lock (mtime 10 min old) and 8 parallel accepts, 2 of 30 trials ended with fewer entries than successful runs, and every run reported success. A stale lock is exactly what a crashed or killed run (Ctrl-C, CI timeout) leaves behind. The lock is also never refreshed while held, so on a slow or network filesystem a run that holds it for more than 30s is treated as stale and broken while it is still writing. The same code is mirrored in .claude/helpers/kit/noise-ledger.js:235.
fix_hint: Break a stale lock atomically: rename it to a unique name such as `${lock}.${pid}.${rand}.stale` and only the run whose rename succeeds removes it and retries; or write a random token into the lock and, in finally, remove it only if it still holds your token. Add a test that runs parallel accepts against a pre-existing stale lock and expects every entry kept.

title: prune now fails on a read-only checkout and creates directories even when nothing expired
detail: prune now always goes through withLock, which runs mkdir -p and creates <ledger>.lock before reading. Before this change, prune with nothing expired only read the file. Checked: on a read-only bind mount holding a valid ledger with no expired entries, prune exits 1 with 'cannot lock ledger ...: EROFS'. With no ledger present, prune now leaves empty .claude/kit/ directories behind. An advisory prune step on a read-only CI workspace or a mounted snapshot breaks for no reason.
fix_hint: In prune, read the ledger first without a lock. Return early when nothing is expired, and take the lock and re-read only when there is something to write.

title: Lock file handle close() is not awaited
detail: (await fs.open(lock, 'wx')).close() drops the promise that close() returns. If close rejects (EIO/EBADF on a flaky network filesystem), the rejection is unhandled and can crash the process (Node >=15 default) after the ledger was already written. Also, nothing guarantees the handle is closed before fn runs. The same code is mirrored in .claude/helpers/kit/noise-ledger.js:231.
fix_hint: const h = await fs.open(lock, 'wx'); await h.close(); break;

title: A bin check whose target is a path always fails
detail: findOnPath joins every PATH entry with the target, so a project check like {"kind":"bin","target":"/bin/sh","fatal":true} or "node_modules/.bin/eslint" looks for <entry>//bin/sh and is reported as '/bin/sh not found on PATH'. Confirmed: with /bin/sh present, doctor exits 2 (refused). parseConfig accepts these targets without complaint, so a user who points a fatal bin check at a pinned path blocks every run with a false failure.
fix_hint: If the target contains a path separator (or is absolute), resolve it against cwd and test it directly for an executable file instead of searching PATH; or reject such targets in parseConfig with exit 1.

title: A json check prints part of the file's contents when the file is malformed
detail: On a parse failure, `found` includes JSON.parse's message, and on Node 20+ that message quotes the text around the error. Confirmed: a file containing {"token": ghp_ABCDEFsecretvalue} yields found = 's.json is not valid JSON (Unexpected token 'g', ..."{"token": ghp_ABCDEF"... is not valid JSON)'. A project json check on a credentials or settings file therefore writes a slice of a secret to stdout (and into marathon logs). The verb promises that env values are never printed, but it gives no such guarantee for file contents, so a user has no reason to expect the leak.
fix_hint: Report only the position (the 'line N column M' / 'position N' part) or a fixed 'is not valid JSON' sentence, never e.message's quoted snippet; add a test with a secret-looking token in a malformed file.

title: Running doctor from a subdirectory falsely reports the kit missing
detail: The file and json checks resolve against io.cwd (process.cwd()), but the git-work-tree check walks upward. From <project>/sub, `node ../.claude/helpers/kit/cli.js doctor` reports '.claude/helpers/kit/cli.js not found' and exits 2. The file it reports as missing is the very script that is running. The marathon profile likewise fails .claude/marathon.json. A user who runs the preflight from a subfolder is refused, and the fix hint ('run danizee-claude-suite install') sends them the wrong way.
fix_hint: Anchor the built-in file/json checks at the project root (the directory holding .claude, found by walking up as inGitWorkTree does, or derived from the kit's own location), or say in the found text which directory was searched.

title: A UTF-8 BOM in doctor.json makes the config invalid
detail: loadConfig (and checkJson) pass the raw text to JSON.parse, so a doctor.json saved with a BOM (the default in some Windows editors) is rejected with exit 1: 'Unexpected token '\uFEFF''. The error shows the BOM as an invisible character, so the user cannot see the cause.
fix_hint: Strip a leading \uFEFF before JSON.parse in loadConfig and checkJson.

title: A record whose element still fires is closed as fixed when a candidate overlaps two live records
detail: visit() matches each candidate to only ONE record (the best overlap, lines 221-229) and adds only that record to `touched`. Any other live record of the same scope+rule that shares members with the candidate is not touched, so the absence loop (line 266) counts it absent even though its members fired. Confirmed: visit s1 [a] -> R1{a}; s2 [b] -> R2{b}; then s3, s4, s5 each see [a,b]: R1 is raised as pending each time and R2 is closed as fixed in s5 with absent_visits 3, while element b fired in every one of those visits. If R2 was filed, `closed` tells the caller to close a tracker issue that is still occurring. This contradicts the header's rule that a record is absent only when none of its members fired.
fix_hint: Mark every record of the same scope+rule that overlaps the candidate's sigs as touched (reset absent_visits) or merge them into the chosen record, not just the best match; add a test with two disjoint records later seen together.

title: A reopened filed issue loses its decision and is raised again every visit without its issue ref
detail: When a fixed record is sighted again, line 241 sets status to 'new'. The reopened raise carries the old issue ref once, but from the next sighting on the record is a plain 'pending' raise with no `issue` field (line 256 only adds it for status 'reopened'), and recurred/occurrence counting for the issue stops. Confirmed: filed GH-1, closed by absence, s5 sighting gives reopened+GH-1, s6 sighting gives status pending with no issue. A caller that syncs `raise` to its tracker will open a duplicate issue for a fingerprint the ledger already filed, which the idea says must not be raised again.
fix_hint: On reopen of a record that has an issue, keep status 'filed' (report it once as reopened) so later sightings go to `recurred` with the issue ref; or always include rec.issue in raise rows.

title: Visit JSON with a UTF-8 BOM is rejected as not valid JSON on both --in and stdin
detail: readInput passes the raw text to JSON.parse, so a file or pipe starting with a UTF-8 BOM (common from Windows editors and PowerShell) fails with 'visit input is not valid JSON' and exit 1, a misleading error for valid JSON. Confirmed with both `--in bom.json` and piped stdin. loadState (line 135) has the same issue for the state file.
fix_hint: Strip a leading \uFEFF before JSON.parse in readInput and loadState.

title: Tool-limit refusals (exit 2) are classified as a blocking regression
detail: Status 2 maps to `regression` (blocks: true) for every verb with no per-verb override. But existing verbs use exit 2 for tool or environment refusals that say nothing about the product: diff-range exits 2 when the review range is over 32 MiB (diff-range.js:340) or the repo config has an include.path (diff-range.js:215), and safe-git exits 2 for every refused argument (safe-git.js:171). Confirmed: `cli.js exit-codes blocks 2 --verb safe-git` and `describe 2 --verb diff-range` both return class regression, blocks true, so a large PR or a refused git option turns the gate red. That is the false red the idea says must never happen. The test at test/kit-exit-code-contract-separating-infrastruc.test.js (`classify({ code: 2, verb: 'safe-git' }).class === 'regression'`) locks this in.
fix_hint: Add overrides for diff-range 2 and safe-git 2 that map to a non-blocking class (usage or precondition), so only verbs whose 2 means a product verdict (e.g. push-gate) block; or make blocking opt-in per verb, and test it.

title: Contract says timeouts and crashes are infrastructure, but they actually exit 1 and are classified as usage
detail: The infrastructure class claims to cover 'timeout, crash, signal, git failure', but nothing in the kit produces 5 for those. cli.js returns 1 for any non-KitExit error (a crash), Node's own uncaught exception exits 1, and diff-range exits 1 when a git child times out or git fails (diff-range.js:9,27,33). So `exit-codes describe 1 --verb diff-range` reports class usage with 'Invalid input ... Fix the caller.' for what is a git timeout. A CI that follows this contract tells people to fix their call when the tool itself failed. That is a wrong classification for a case the contract names.
fix_hint: Either describe 1 as 'usage or tool failure (not separable yet)', or add a diff-range 1 override and note that crashes surface as 1 until cli.js maps non-KitExit errors to 5. Add a test for the diff-range timeout path.

title: `--flag=value` form is refused, unlike sibling verbs
detail: diff-range (diff-range.js:95), safe-git and scrub accept `--name=value`, but exit-codes only accepts `--verb v`: `cli.js exit-codes describe 2 --verb=safe-git` exits 1 with 'unknown option --verb=safe-git'. A CI step written in the style the other verbs accept fails loudly instead of classifying. `describe --help` is also refused as an unknown option.
fix_hint: In parse, split an `--name=value` argument at the first '=' and handle it like the two-argument form; add a test.

title: planTests ignores input.changed, so the module entry returns an empty, confident plan
detail: validateInput accepts a top-level "changed" key and the header says changed files come from it, but only run() (line 237) reads input.changed. planTests builds its file list from the second argument alone. A code caller using the module entry, as the brief asks, with planTests({targets:[{id:'a',files:['x.js']}], changed:['x.js']}) gets plan [], changed_total 0 and low_confidence false. Nothing is tested and nothing is flagged, which is the silent under-testing the idea rules out.
fix_hint: In planTests, merge input.changed with the changed argument (as run does), or reject a call where input.changed is set and the argument is also given. Add a unit test for planTests(input) with input.changed.

title: The flows type check runs after the loop, so a non-list flows crashes with a raw TypeError
detail: Line 67 iterates input.flows before line 73 checks that it is a list. With flows:{} the CLI prints 'kit: object is not iterable (cannot read property Symbol(Symbol.iterator))' rather than '"flows" must be a list (see --help)'. With flows:"ab" it reports 'every flow needs a string "id"'. planTests(input, 'x.js'), where changed is a string and not a list, also throws a raw TypeError ('(changed ?? []).map is not a function'). The exit code is still 1, but the message does not tell the user what to fix.
fix_hint: Move the Array.isArray(input.flows) check above the loop, as is done for edges. In planTests, reject a changed value that is not an array, with a KitExit.

title: No change source at all exits 0 with an empty plan and low_confidence false
detail: If none of input.changed, --changed or --diff is given (for example a CI step that forgot --diff, or an empty diff file from a wrong git range), files is empty. Rule 4 then skips the smoke set and the flag, and the verb exits 0 with only the always items. The header documents this, but a caller cannot tell 'nothing changed' from 'no change input reached the verb', and the job that is meant to fall back to a smoke set reports nothing to test.
fix_hint: In run(), exit 1 when no change source was given at all. Alternatively, add a field such as change_source:'none' or a low_confidence_reason so that an empty change set is visible.

title: Stale-lock break can steal a live lock, so two writers run at once and a spend is lost
detail: When the lock is older than LOCK_STALE_MS, each waiter that stat()ed it renames whatever is at <state>.lock away. Waiter A can break the stale lock and create its own fresh lock; waiter B, which stat()ed the old lock just before, then renames A's fresh lock away and takes its own. A and B both run load..save together, and the finally check (token mismatch) hides it. Confirmed: crashed-holder recovery (lock file aged 2 min, then 20 parallel `spend --steps 1` processes), repeated 15 times. One trial ended with spent.steps=19 of 20 and every process exited 0. This is the recovery path after a sub-agent dies holding the lock, and it brings back the round-1 lost-update bug with no error. Mirrored in .claude/helpers/kit/shared-budget.js.
fix_hint: Break a stale lock only if it is still the same file you judged stale. Read its token/ino before the rename, rename it to a unique name, then check that the renamed file has that token/ino; if not, rename it back or treat it as live. Or use a lock dir with an owner pid and check the pid is alive. Add a test that pre-ages the lock and runs N parallel spends, asserting spent.steps === N.

title: A grant reserves the whole remainder, so parallel sub-sessions are skipped and a crashed one blocks the budget
detail: grantFor returns everything still available, and recordGrant reserves all of it on the helper row. The first helper granted therefore holds 100% of steps and cost. Every other model grant made before that helper spends is skipped with 'fully reserved by other sub-sessions'. Confirmed: open --steps 10 --cost 5, grant A returns {steps:10,cost:5}, then grant B returns skip:true. Fan-out, the 'several sub-agents share one allowance' use case, degrades to one model sub-session at a time. On the failure path it is worse: a sub-session that is killed or crashes before calling spend keeps its reservation forever (no expiry, no release verb). Every later model grant is then skipped until someone sends a manual `spend --steps 0` for that helper id, which the docs and usage do not mention.
fix_hint: Let a grant ask for a bounded share (e.g. --steps/--cost on grant, or --parts N that splits what is available) and reserve only that share. Document and test releasing a dead helper's reservation, for example `spend --steps 0 --outcome failed`, or add a `release` command.

title: Lock wait (10 s) is shorter than stale age (30 s), so calls fail for ~30 s after a crashed holder and spends are dropped
detail: If a process dies holding <state>.lock, every grant, start, stop and spend in the next ~30 s gives up after LOCK_WAIT_MS=10000 with exit 1 ('budget state is locked'), because the lock is not stale yet. Confirmed: with a leftover lock file, a `spend --steps 3 --outcome failed` failed after 10024 ms and spent stayed 0. That spend is never recorded, against 'spend is recorded at once, failures included'. The window is narrow because the lock is held only for milliseconds, but the result is lost accounting.
fix_hint: Make LOCK_WAIT_MS longer than LOCK_STALE_MS (or shorten the stale age to a few seconds, since the lock is held only for one read-modify-write) so a waiter always reaches the stale-break path before giving up.

title: Secret containing a quote or backslash leaks through the 'repeated' line
detail: The repeated-call line embeds stable(s.input), which is JSON.stringify output, so a '"' or '\' inside a secret is escaped (\" / \\) before redactSecrets runs on line 172. The escaped form no longer matches the secret, so it reaches the trouble log in clear. Confirmed: secret 'pa\ss"w0rd-LONGSECRET' passed in secrets, two identical Bash calls with input {command:'login '+secret} give the line 'repeated: Bash 2 times with identical input {"command":"login pa\\ss\"w0rd-LONGSECRET"}'. Generated passwords often contain these characters, and this output is what the reviewer model gets.
fix_hint: Redact the raw input values before serialising them (walk the input and redactSecrets each string), or also redact using the JSON-escaped form of each secret (JSON.stringify(s).slice(1,-1)); add a test with a quote/backslash secret.

title: 'Same field typed into again' never fires for MCP or computer-use typing tools
detail: EDIT_TOOL is anchored (^...$), so tool names as they appear in Claude Code transcripts, such as mcp__playwright__browser_type or browser_fill_form, never match. The computer tool with action:'type' does not match either. Confirmed: three mcp__playwright__browser_type calls into element 'Email' / ref 'e12' with different text produce only 'stop: unknown'. The idea lists the typed-into-field signal, and through the transcript input it only works for Edit/Write file edits.
fix_hint: Match the last segment after an mcp__<server>__ prefix (e.g. /(^|__)(browser_)?(type|fill(_form)?|...)$/i) and treat {name:'computer', input.action:'type'} as a typing call; add a transcript test.

title: Imperative check refuses verbs ending in 'ing' (Bring, Ping)
detail: /ing$/i on the first word is meant to catch gerunds but also rejects real imperatives. Confirmed: 'Bring the server up before running e2e tests.' and 'Ping the health endpoint before deploying.' both exit 1 with 'a lesson is imperative: start with a verb, not "Bring"'. The reviewer has to reword a valid lesson.
fix_hint: Allow a small list of -ing verbs (bring, ping, string, sing, ring, swing, cling, fling, sting, wring), or only reject -ing words longer than 5 letters that are not on that list.

title: Hard per-session cap on new lessons applies only when --session is passed
detail: The cap check only runs when opts.session is set, and --session is optional with no default. A workflow that calls 'reflect lessons save' without --session can save any number of new lessons, but the idea calls this a hard per-session cap. Nothing warns about it and nothing in the usage marks --session as needed for the cap.
fix_hint: Require --session on save (exit 1 without it), or fall back to an env/session id the caller always has, and test that a save without a session cannot go over the cap.

title: Abbreviations like 'e.g.' count as a second sentence
detail: /[.!?]\s+\S/ treats any period followed by a space as a sentence end. Confirmed: 'Use npm ci, e.g. in CI jobs.' is refused with 'a lesson is ONE sentence'.
fix_hint: Ignore common abbreviations (e.g., i.e., etc., vs.) before the sentence test, or only flag a period followed by a space and an upper-case letter.

title: Test name says a fresh lock times out as exit 1, but nothing asserts it
detail: 'a stale lock is broken; a fresh lock times out as exit 1' only covers the stale-lock case. The timeout path in withLock (reflect.js:259) is never run, so it could hang or return the wrong code and this test would still pass.
fix_hint: Call withLock on a fresh lock file with a small waitMs (e.g. 100) and assert it rejects with code 1 and leaves the lock in place.

title: Library input: non-JSON run values compare as equal, so differing runs block
detail: Through the library entry gate(), checkRun (line 53) accepts any value in checks/outputs, and canon() treats every non-array object as a plain object by its own keys. A Date, Map or Set has no own keys, so it canonicalises to "{}". Two runs whose outputs are {at: new Date(0)} and {at: new Date(9e12)}, or {m: Map{1=>2}} and {m: Map{1=>3}}, come back as `blocking` with exit 2 (confirmed with a node one-liner). Flaky runs then fail the gate, which is the one thing the verb exists to prevent. Also [undefined] and [null] compare equal, and a BigInt makes JSON.stringify throw a bare TypeError rather than KitExit 1. The CLI is safe because JSON.parse only produces plain values. The library path is the documented entry for code callers.
fix_hint: In checkRun, require checks, outputs and steps to be plain JSON: walk the value and fail with KitExit 1 on any object whose prototype is not Object.prototype or null, and on non-finite numbers, bigint, undefined, functions and symbols. Add a library test with Date and Map outputs.

title: Malformed replay result aborts the whole batch, but a throwing replay only downgrades its own verdict
detail: When the injected replay throws, that verdict becomes `untested` and the rest of the batch is still judged. When it returns a malformed run instead (for example {} or a run with an extra key), checkRun throws KitExit 1 from inside the loop. Every other verdict's result is then discarded, including real `blocking` ones, and the exit becomes 1 instead of 2. Bad replay output from one claim hides an agreed failure on another claim.
fix_hint: Wrap the checkRun of the replay result in the same try as the replay call, and classify a bad run as `untested` with the validation message as the reason. Keep KitExit 1 for invalid caller input only.

title: --file - is read as a file named '-' rather than stdin, and a repeated --file silently wins
detail: Sibling kit verbs (graph.js:1360, lenses.js:366) treat '-' as stdin. Here `replay-gate --file -` fails with "cannot read -: ENOENT". Given `--file a.json --file b.json`, the verb quietly uses b.json with no error.
fix_hint: Treat '-' as stdin to match the other verbs, or reject it with a clear message. Reject a second --file.

title: Comment says 'Clear - no blocking findings' while JUnit fails and SARIF reports an error for the same input
detail: renderComment counts only blocking findings with disposition 'open' (line 212), but renderJunit (line 166) and renderSarif (line 97) treat every blocking finding as a failure or error whatever its disposition. Input {findings:[{id:'x',message:'sql inj',severity:'blocking',disposition:'filed'}]} renders the comment verdict '**Clear** - no blocking findings (0 advisory, 1 filed)', while the JUnit has failures="1" and the SARIF has level 'error'. A blocking finding marked needs-decision gets 'Needs a decision' in the comment and still fails the JUnit. The PR comment says there are no blocking findings while the CI check built from the same findings is red. The envelope's counts.blocking (line 82) also counts the filed one, so it disagrees with the comment too.
fix_hint: Pick one rule and apply it in all three renderers. Either have JUnit and SARIF demote filed and needs-decision blocking findings the same way the comment does, or keep them blocking and change the comment verdict to say 'no open blocking findings (N blocking filed)'. Add a test that renders one filed blocking finding in all three formats.

title: SARIF results with no file have no locations, and GitHub code scanning rejects the whole upload
detail: A finding without `file` is a valid input and is the 'orphan' case the brief says to keep, but it becomes a SARIF result with no `locations` array (lines 101-105). It can also have no ruleId when `id` is missing (line 98). GitHub code scanning refuses such files with 'locationFromSarifResult: expected at least one location', so a single orphan finding makes the SARIF upload in the test.yml target fail. The packaged test passes a fileless finding ('orphan') and checks only the levels, so it does not catch this.
fix_hint: When a finding has no file, emit a fallback location (for example artifactLocation.uri of the repo root or the tool's config file, or a logicalLocation plus a placeholder physicalLocation) and a fallback ruleId such as 'finding'. Add a test that every result has locations[0] and a ruleId.

title: Orphan findings and the incomplete-run error merge into user tests in the reserved suites
detail: Orphan findings go into the suite 'unattributed' under the name f.id, and the incomplete error goes into suite 'run' under the name 'run-completed'. Both use the same slot map as the user's tests, so a listed test {name:'x',suite:'unattributed'} takes over orphan finding id 'x' and fails. A listed test {name:'run-completed',suite:'run'} takes over the incomplete-run error. A real test case is then blamed for a finding or error it did not produce.
fix_hint: Keep the reserved suites separate from user suites, for example by giving them their own Map or rejecting tests[].suite equal to 'unattributed' or 'run' in normalize.

title: render never emits a writable SARIF or JUnit file; output is always the JSON envelope
detail: run returns { format, incomplete, counts, content }, so `cli.js render junit > junit.xml` writes JSON, not XML. For SARIF it writes the envelope, not the SARIF log. Every CI caller has to extract .content with jq before upload-sarif or a JUnit reporter can read it. cli.js already supports a `raw` result for exactly this case.
fix_hint: Add an --out <file> flag that writes content to a file (or a --raw flag that returns { raw: content }), and keep the envelope as the default.

title: An empty --diff or --changed file still gives a confident, empty plan with exit 0
detail: The new guard rejects only a run with no change flag at all. The case named in r2 is still open: an empty diff file from a wrong git range. On a degraded or shallow CI checkout, `git fetch origin main` fails, so `git diff origin/main...HEAD > d.diff` leaves an empty file. That file passes the guard, and line 253 lets an empty text through. Confirmed: run(['--diff','empty.diff']) and run(['--changed','empty.diff']) both return plan [], changed_total 0, low_confidence false, exit 0. The advisory CI job then reports nothing to test, with no smoke set and no flag. A caller cannot tell 'nothing changed' from 'the change input never arrived', which is the silent under-testing the brief rules out. The same applies to .claude/helpers/kit/test-plan.js:238.
fix_hint: When every change source given resolves to zero paths (an empty or whitespace-only --diff or --changed file), set low_confidence: true with a reason such as 'change source was empty' and add the smoke set, or exit 1 unless an explicit flag like --allow-empty is passed. Keep the explicit input.changed: [] case as it is now. Add a test for an empty --diff file.

title: planTests now throws on blank entries, which the CLI path and the old code filtered out
detail:
The new strList check on the changed argument rejects empty or whitespace-only strings. The usual code-caller input is `execSync('git diff --name-only').toString().split('
')`, which always ends in ''. Confirmed: planTests({targets:[{id:'a',files:['x.js']}]}, 'x.js
'.split('
')) throws 'the changed argument must be a list of non-empty strings (see --help)'. Before this commit the entry was dropped by .filter(Boolean). run() filters blank lines from a --changed file (line 248), so the module entry is now stricter than the CLI for the same data. The '(see --help)' suffix also means nothing to a module caller. The same applies to .claude/helpers/kit/test-plan.js:102.
fix_hint: Check only that changed is an array of strings, and keep dropping blanks with the existing normPath/filter(Boolean). Or document that callers must filter blanks first, and give module callers an error message without the --help suffix.

title: Tool-limit refusals (exit 2) of graph, impact and callers still classify as a blocking regression
detail: The r1 fix added exit-2 overrides only for safe-git and diff-range, but the kit's KitExit contract makes 2 a policy refusal for every verb, and other verbs use it for tool limits that say nothing about the product. Confirmed: a diff over 32 MiB makes `cli.js graph --diff big.diff`, `impact --diff big.diff` and `callers --diff big.diff` exit 2 ('refused: ... is larger than 33554432 bytes', graph.js:1367/1370), and `cli.js exit-codes blocks 2 --verb graph` / `--verb impact` / `--verb callers` all return class regression, blocks true. guarded-fs refusals (symlink, path swapped, file too large; guarded-fs.js:53) and scrub's file-count limits (scrub.js:232,333) take the same path. A large PR or a raced folder turns the gate red, the false red the idea says must never happen.
fix_hint: Invert the default: make exit 2 non-blocking (precondition/refusal) unless the verb is listed as a product judge (e.g. push-gate), or add 2→precondition overrides for graph, impact, callers and every verb that refuses via guarded-fs or a size limit, with tests.

title: A misspelled --verb silently falls back to the defaults, so a typo can make a refusal block
detail: toVerb checks only the shape of the name. `exit-codes blocks 2 --verb safegit` (typo for safe-git) returns class regression, blocks true with no warning, whereas `--verb safe-git` returns precondition, blocks false. A CI step with a typo turns safe-git's argument refusals into blocking regressions and gives no error.
fix_hint: Reject a --verb that is not a registered kit verb (or at least add `known_verb: false` / a warning in the JSON) and test the typo case.

title: `exit-codes table --help` is refused as an unknown option
detail: run() parses `table` arguments before the --help check, so `cli.js exit-codes table --help` exits 1 with 'unknown option --help', while `describe --help`, `blocks --help` and `classify --help` print usage. The --help branch lists 'table' but cannot be reached for it.
fix_hint: Move the `rest.includes('--help')` check above the `table` branch; add a test.

title: Shell statuses 126/127 (tool not executable / not found) are reported as unknown instead of precondition
detail: `exit-codes classify --code 127` returns class unknown, 'not a verified regression. Treat it as an unclassified failure.' When CI runs the kit and the binary or node is missing, the shell returns 127 (126 when not executable): the exact 'missing tool' precondition the contract defines class 4 for. The contract tells CI it cannot tell a broken tool from a broken product in the most common broken-tool case.
fix_hint: Map 126 and 127 to precondition (or infrastructure) with a description naming the shell meaning, and test it.

title: Stale-lock break can still remove a fresh lock, so two runs hold it and an accept is lost
detail: withLock decides the lock is stale from fs.stat (line 258) and only afterwards reads its token (readToken), which it passes to breakStale as 'seen'. If another waiter breaks the dead lock and creates its own fresh lock between that stat and that read, this waiter reads the new holder's token. breakStale then re-reads the same token, finds it unchanged (line 240) and deletes the live lock. Both runs then do the read-modify-write and the last rename wins. Every run still reports success. The token check proves only that the content did not change between the two reads. It does not prove that the lock read is the stale one. Checked: with a pre-aged ledger.json.lock and 8 parallel accepts, plus 0-15 ms of latency added after fs.stat (as on a slow or network filesystem or a loaded CI host), 2 of 30 trials ended with 7 entries after 8 successful runs. Without the added latency, 0 of 300 trials failed, so the existing tests do not catch it. The same code is mirrored in .claude/helpers/kit/noise-ledger.js. This is the round 3 finding, narrowed but not closed.
fix_hint: After taking <lock>.break in breakStale, stat the lock again and remove it only if it is still older than LOCK_STALE_MS and still holds the token 'seen'. The holder's heartbeat and a just-created lock both make it fresh. Add a test that injects a delay after stat, for example by wrapping fs.stat, and expects every entry kept.

title: --config targets resolve against the project root, not the cwd the config path was resolved from, and the failure does not say where it looked
detail: loadConfig resolves an explicit --config path against io.cwd (line 201), but customCheck anchors every file/json/bin target at findProjectRoot(cwd) (line 213). Confirmed: from <project>/sub with sub/my.json = {checks:[{name:'x',kind:'file',target:'here.txt',fatal:true}]} and sub/here.txt present, `doctor --config my.json` exits 2 with found 'here.txt not found'. A config kept beside a sub-package blocks the run with a false fatal failure, and the found/fix text ('Create here.txt.') sends the user to create a file that already exists, with no hint which directory was searched. Neither the header nor usage says targets are root-relative.
fix_hint: Say in usage/header that project-check targets are relative to the project root, and name the resolved directory (or the root) in the found text of failing file/json/bin path checks; add a test for --config from a subdirectory.

title: A project check name valid under one profile makes another profile exit 1
detail: The built-in collision check only knows the names of the current profile. Confirmed: doctor.json with a check named 'bin:claude' passes `doctor` (exit 0) but `doctor --profile marathon` throws 'collides with a built-in check' (exit 1), so the config the user validated blocks the marathon preflight as invalid input.
fix_hint: Reject in parseConfig (or runDoctor) any project name that matches a built-in name from any profile, so the error shows on the first run.

title: A nested repo without the kit inherits the outer project's kit, config and marathon.json
detail: findProjectRoot searches every ancestor for .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js before it looks for the nearest .git. Confirmed: <outer> with the kit and <outer>/inner/.git (no kit): doctor run with cwd inner reports 'file:.claude/helpers/kit/cli.js present', loads <outer>/.claude/kit/doctor.json and would check <outer>/.claude/marathon.json, exit 0. The fatal kit-present check cannot fail for an inner repo.
fix_hint: Stop the kit-marker walk at the nearest .git boundary (search for both markers in one upward walk and take the first directory holding either).

title: A file check whose target is a directory says 'not found'
detail: isFile returns false for a directory, so checkFile reports '<rel> not found' and fix 'Create <rel>.' when the path exists as a folder; the user is told to create something that is already there.
fix_hint: stat once and report '<rel> is a directory, not a file' when it exists but is not a regular file.

title: Packaged marathon run accepts either exit code
detail: assert.ok([0, 2].includes(mara.code)) plus a row-shape check passes whether marathon's fatal checks run or not; a packaged build that dropped the marathon.json or git-tree checks would still pass.
fix_hint: Assert the specific failed list (e.g. that json:.claude/marathon.json is in failed and exit is 2 when it is absent) and that bin:claude is advisory.
